plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Hold there, traveller. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. Straight down this road to the square. It’s the tall house with the lantern.
plan.say: Hold there, traveller. Bracken-fell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Gretta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. Straight down this road to the square. It's the tall house with the lantern.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: You lit the harvest fire. I never thought to see it burn again. You’re one of us now, whether you like it or not.
plan.say: You lit the harvest fire. I never thought to see it burn again. You're one of us now, whether you like it or not.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Road’s quiet. Just how I like it.
plan.say: Road's quiet. Just how I like it.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: The old watchtower, up the crag to the north-east. It held a beacon once. Burned out before my grandfather’s day. Children dare each other up there, though they swear to me they don’t.
plan.say: The old watchtower, up the crag to the north-east. It held a beacon once. Burned out before my grandfather's day. Children dare each other up there, though they swear to me they don't.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Last village before the Greyspine passes. Sixty souls, one inn, one forge, and a chapel bell that no longer rings. Mind the river. The Stonewater is colder than she looks, and she doesn’t give back what she takes.
plan.say: Last village before the Grey-spine passes. Sixty souls, one inn, one forge, and a chapel bell that no longer rings. Mind the river. The Stone-water is colder than she looks, and she doesn't give back what she takes.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Well now, a new face! Hale sent you? Then you’re welcome under this roof. There’s a bed up the stairs, by the window. It’s yours while you stay. But I’ll ask a kindness in return. Osric at the mill owes me a sack of malt, and I can’t brew on promises. Fetch it for me?
plan.say: Well now, a new face! Hale sent you? Then you're welcome under this roof. There's a bed up the stairs, by the window. It's yours while you stay. But I'll ask a kindness in return. Ozrick at the mill owes me a sack of malt, and I can't brew on promises. Fetch it for me?

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: You’re a treasure. Over the bridge east of the square, then follow the river downstream. You’ll hear the wheel before you see it.
plan.say: You're a treasure. Over the bridge east of the square, then follow the river downstream. You'll hear the wheel before you see it.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The mill is over the bridge east of the square, then down the river. Osric will know what I’m owed.
plan.say: The mill is over the bridge east of the square, then down the river. Ozrick will know what I'm owed.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: That’s the malt! Oh, bless you. There’ll be ale by week’s end. Here, for your trouble, and a bottle of the last batch.
plan.say: That's the malt! Oh, bless you. There'll be ale by week's end. Here, for your trouble, and a bottle of the last batch.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: If you’ve a mind to stay useful: Brandt has been storming about since his hammer went missing, old Maren is short of frostcaps, and Brother Aldous frets over that silent bell of his. And the Elder likes company, out under the oak.
plan.say: If you've a mind to stay useful: Brant has been storming about since his hammer went missing, old Marren is short of frost-caps, and Brother Awldus frets over that silent bell of his. And the Elder likes company, out under the oak.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: The whole village in my hall, and the fire lit in the square. I could weep. Sit, drink!
plan.say: The whole village in my hall, and the fire lit in the square. I could weep. Sit, drink!

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: What can I get you, love?
plan.say: What can I get you, love?

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: It’s two gold, love, and your purse is light. Help a few folk around the village and come back.
plan.say: It's two gold, love, and your purse is light. Help a few folk around the village and come back.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Warm, and sweet with heather honey. The room feels friendlier already.
plan.say: Warm, and sweet with heather honey. The room feels friendlier already.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Three generations of Barleybrooks have kept this hearth. The beams came down from the beacon forest, and the recipe for the ale came from my gran, who took it from a traveller in trade for a night’s lodging. So you see, I’ve a soft spot for strangers.
plan.say: Three generations of Barley-brooks have kept this hearth. The beams came down from the beacon forest, and the recipe for the ale came from my gran, who took it from a traveller in trade for a night's lodging. So you see, I've a soft spot for strangers.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Up the stairs at the back, the bed by the window. Sleep as late as you like.
plan.say: Up the stairs at the back, the bed by the window. Sleep as late as you like.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Do me one small favour first and there’s a bed in it for you.
plan.say: Do me one small favour first and there's a bed in it for you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Unless you’ve come to tell me where my hammer is, I’ve work to do. My best cross-peen, gone from the bench three days back. And that boy Tobin can’t look me in the eye.
plan.say: Unless you've come to tell me where my hammer is, I've work to do. My best cross-peen, gone from the bench three days back. And that boy Tobbin can't look me in the eye.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Hm. Start with the boy. He’s always underfoot in the square, when he should be at the bellows.
plan.say: Hm. Start with the boy. He's always underfoot in the square, when he should be at the bellows.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: That’s her! Where was she? The watchtower? I’ll tan his... no. No, I was a boy once, and that tower was a castle then too. Take this. I made it for no one in particular, and it seems that was you.
plan.say: That's her! Where was she? The watchtower? I'll tan his... no. No, I was a boy once, and that tower was a castle then too. Take this. I made it for no one in particular, and it seems that was you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: She rings true again. Hear that? That’s the sound of a village with a working forge.
plan.say: She rings true again. Hear that? That's the sound of a village with a working forge.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Find the boy. Tobin. Fair hair, guilty face.
plan.say: Find the boy. Tobbin. Fair hair, guilty face.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: The watchtower, he said? Up the crag past the chapel. Mind your footing.
plan.say: The watchtower, he said? Up the crag past the chapel. Mind your footing.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Iron from the Greyspine, charcoal from the pine, water from the Stonewater. Everything in this valley was made within sight of it. That’s rarer than you’d think.
plan.say: Iron from the Grey-spine, charcoal from the pine, water from the Stone-water. Everything in this valley was made within sight of it. That's rarer than you'd think.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Hm. Young eyes. Good. The frost came early and my stores are thin. I need frostcaps: pale blue, and they glow a little at dusk. They grow where it is cold and quiet. By the lake, at the forest’s edge, near old stones. Bring me five.
plan.say: Hm. Young eyes. Good. The frost came early and my stores are thin. I need frost-caps: pale blue, and they glow a little at dusk. They grow where it is cold and quiet. By the lake, at the forest's edge, near old stones. Bring me five.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Five, and not one bruised! You have gentle hands. Take this tonic. It will keep the mountain chill from your bones.
plan.say: Five, and not one bruised! You have gentle hands. Take this tonic. It will keep the mountain chill from your bones.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Sixty winters in this valley. I have buried more secrets in that garden than turnips.
plan.say: Sixty winters in this valley. I have buried more secrets in that garden than turnips.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Fevers, mostly. And grief, a little, though I don’t tell them that’s what’s in the tea.
plan.say: Fevers, mostly. And grief, a little, though I don't tell them that's what's in the tea.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The peace of the Dawn upon you. Forgive the quiet. Our bell rope rotted through at midsummer, and I have neither the coin nor the knees to replace it. A village without its bell is a body without a voice.
plan.say: The peace of the Dawn upon you. Forgive the quiet. Our bell rope rotted through at midsummer, and I have neither the coin nor the knees to replace it. A village without its bell is a body without a voice.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Would you? Marta keeps good hemp at her shop on the square. The Dawn remembers a kindness.
plan.say: Would you? Marta keeps good hemp at her shop on the square. The Dawn remembers a kindness.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Hemp, and well laid! Give me one moment in the tower... there. It is done. Would you ring it? It ought to be a friend who rings it first.
plan.say: Hemp, and well laid! Give me one moment in the tower... there. It is done. Would you ring it? It ought to be a friend who rings it first.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Marta keeps good hemp rope at her shop on the square, east side.
plan.say: Marta keeps good hemp rope at her shop on the square, east side.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The rope hangs under the tower, by the door. Pull, and let the valley hear.
plan.say: The rope hangs under the tower, by the door. Pull, and let the valley hear.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Listen. The valley has its voice again.
plan.say: Listen. The valley has its voice again.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Only that the night ends. Every night, without fail. We find that worth a small stone house and a bell.
plan.say: Only that the night ends. Every night, without fail. We find that worth a small stone house and a bell.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Quill’s Sundries. If I don’t have it, you don’t need it.
plan.say: Quill's Sundries. If I don't have it, you don't need it.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Thirty feet of the best. Don’t hang anything you can’t lift.
plan.say: Thirty feet of the best. Don't hang anything you can't lift.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Baked this morning. Mostly.
plan.say: Baked this morning. Mostly.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: From Edda’s trees. Sweetest in the valley.
plan.say: From Edda's trees. Sweetest in the valley.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: I trade with the lowland caravans twice a year. The rest of the time I trade in gossip, and the price is always fair.
plan.say: I trade with the lowland caravans twice a year. The rest of the time I trade in gossip, and the price is always fair.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Brackenfell remembers its friends. Stay as long as you like. Stay for good, if the road will let you.
plan.say: Bracken-fell remembers its friends. Stay as long as you like. Stay for good, if the road will let you.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: The inn has its ale, the forge its hammer, Maren her remedies, and the bell its voice. Do you know how long it has been since Brackenfell was whole? We used to light a fire in the square at harvest’s end, and the whole valley would come. Light it tonight. You have earned the tinder.
plan.say: The inn has its ale, the forge its hammer, Marren her remedies, and the bell its voice. Do you know how long it has been since Bracken-fell was whole? We used to light a fire in the square at harvest's end, and the whole valley would come. Light it tonight. You have earned the tinder.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Sit a while. An old man’s stories are all the entertainment this square can afford.
plan.say: Sit a while. An old man's stories are all the entertainment this square can afford.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Before the bell there was the beacon on the crag, and before the beacon, only the stars. We have always found some way to say: here we are. Come and find us.
plan.say: Before the bell there was the beacon on the crag, and before the beacon, only the stars. We have always found some way to say: here we are. Come and find us.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Begin with Greta at the inn. Everything in Brackenfell begins there.
plan.say: Begin with Gretta at the inn. Everything in Bracken-fell begins there.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Safer than most. But there has been smoke in the pines north-west of the gate these three nights, and it is not Wren’s. Outlaws, come down off the passes before the snow. Hale cannot leave the gate, and I am too old to do more than worry. If you carry a blade and know its use, drive them off. Mind the big one.
plan.say: Safer than most. But there has been smoke in the pines north-west of the gate these three nights, and it is not Wren's. Outlaws, come down off the passes before the snow. Hale cannot leave the gate, and I am too old to do more than worry. If you carry a blade and know its use, drive them off. Mind the big one.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: North-west of the gate, among the pines. You will see their rag on a pole before they see you, if you are careful. Eat before you go, and do not be too proud to run.
plan.say: North-west of the gate, among the pines. You will see their rag on a pole before they see you, if you are careful. Eat before you go, and do not be too proud to run.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Then the children can pick berries at the wood’s edge again. This was my father’s, and it has hung on the wall long enough. Take it, with the village’s thanks.
plan.say: Then the children can pick berries at the wood's edge again. This was my father's, and it has hung on the wall long enough. Take it, with the village's thanks.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Troubled me? They had my second-best tongs and a roll of files off the cart at the ford, a week gone. Their chief wears them on his belt like trophies. One ear, red beard. They camp west of the path up to the old watchtower. Bring my tools back and I’ll put a proper sword in your hand, not that kitchen iron.
plan.say: Troubled me? They had my second-best tongs and a roll of files off the cart at the ford, a week gone. Their chief wears them on his belt like trophies. One ear, red beard. They camp west of the path up to the old watchtower. Bring my tools back and I'll put a proper sword in your hand, not that kitchen iron.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Hah! Not a scratch on them. As promised: an arming sword, drawn out this spring and waiting for a hand. Keep the point low and your feet moving.
plan.say: Hah! Not a scratch on them. As promised: an arming sword, drawn out this spring and waiting for a hand. Keep the point low and your feet moving.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: There’s coin on the board for outlaws, and I’ll pay it myself. Five of them put down and the road is a road again. Two camps: one in the pines north-west of here, one under the old watchtower. Don’t take on more than you can see.
plan.say: There's coin on the board for outlaws, and I'll pay it myself. Five of them put down and the road is a road again. Two camps: one in the pines north-west of here, one under the old watchtower. Don't take on more than you can see.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Five, by my count and yours. Paid in full. You’ve done the valley a turn, and I’ll not forget it.
plan.say: Five, by my count and yours. Paid in full. You've done the valley a turn, and I'll not forget it.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Twenty-four, child. Frostcaps do not pick themselves.
plan.say: Twenty-four, child. frost-caps do not pick themselves.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Drink it when you bleed, not before. It is no use against foolishness.
plan.say: Drink it when you bleed, not before. It is no use against foolishness.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Since you are the sort who walks: I have a tea I used to make from three herbs and my knees now refuse. Bogbean from the hermit’s pool, sunwort from the bee meadow, stonecrop from the old stones on the eastern hill. It is the only thing that lets Edda’s widow sleep.
plan.say: Since you are the sort who walks: I have a tea I used to make from three herbs and my knees now refuse. bog-bean from the hermit's pool, sun-wort from the bee meadow, stone-crop from the old stones on the eastern hill. It is the only thing that lets Edda's widow sleep.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: All three. And the stonecrop still wet. Sit, sit. I will brew it now, and you shall have the first cup.
plan.say: All three. And the stone-crop still wet. Sit, sit. I will brew it now, and you shall have the first cup.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Where did you… that is Corwin’s cap. Hob’s brother went down the old mine after silver, a good while back. So. It is the end of a long hope. Thank you for bringing it home rather than leaving it to the damp.
plan.say: Where did you... that is Corwin's cap. Hob's brother went down the old mine after silver, a good while back. So. It is the end of a long hope. Thank you for bringing it home rather than leaving it to the damp.

plan.speaker: rowan
plan.text: Corwin the miner. He went into the old workings south-west of here after silver; his brother Hob was the last to see him. The Warden barred the door afterwards. If you come across anything of his, I would be glad of it.
plan.say: Corwin the miner. He went into the old workings south-west of here after silver; his brother Hob was the last to see him. The Warden barred the door afterwards. If you come across anything of his, I would be glad of it.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Sound work, that. Look after it and it will look after you.
plan.say: Sound work, that. Look after it and it will look after you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Iron from the Greyspine, every piece. I don’t haggle.
plan.say: Iron from the Grey-spine, every piece. I don't haggle.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Let’s see it, then.
plan.say: Let's see it, then.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: You’ve nothing I’d give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.
plan.say: You've nothing I'd give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: Greta’s malt! I’d clean forgot, what with the wheel groaning all week. Here, take it, and tell her the next sack is on me. I’d carry it myself, but the stones won’t dress themselves.
plan.say: Gretta's malt! I'd clean forgot, what with the wheel groaning all week. Here, take it, and tell her the next sack is on me. I'd carry it myself, but the stones won't dress themselves.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: Mind the dust. A mill is no place for a naked flame, or a fool.
plan.say: Mind the dust. A mill is no place for a naked flame, or a fool.

plan.speaker: osric
plan.text: The Stonewater turns my wheel, the wheel turns the stones, and the stones feed the valley. Simple as bread. Listen: you can hear her running true.
plan.say: The Stone-water turns my wheel, the wheel turns the stones, and the stones feed the valley. Simple as bread. Listen: you can hear her running true.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: The hammer? I, um. I only borrowed it! I was playing knights up at the old watchtower, and then it got dark, and I ran, and... I left it by the fire ring. Please don’t tell him it was me.
plan.say: The hammer? I, um. I only borrowed it! I was playing knights up at the old watchtower, and then it got dark, and I ran, and... I left it by the fire ring. Please don't tell him it was me.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: He wasn’t even cross! Well. He was a bit cross.
plan.say: He wasn't even cross! Well. He was a bit cross.

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: Bet you can’t beat me to the well!
plan.say: Bet you can't beat me to the well!

plan.speaker: tobin
plan.text: A smith, like Brandt. I’m going to forge a sword as tall as Warden Hale. Taller!
plan.say: A smith, like Brant. I'm going to forge a sword as tall as Warden Hale. Taller!

plan.speaker: edda
plan.text: Wheat’s in, mostly. Chickens are out, always.
plan.say: Wheat's in, mostly. Chickens are out, always.

plan.speaker: edda
plan.text: Fairweather land, five generations. The soil is thin and the summers short, but the bread tastes of it. If you see Bram dawdling at the market, tell him the barn won’t sweep itself.
plan.say: Fair-weather land, five generations. The soil is thin and the summers short, but the bread tastes of it. If you see Bram dawdling at the market, tell him the barn won't sweep itself.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Shh. You’ll scare the char.
plan.say: Shh. You'll scare the char.

plan.speaker: finn
plan.text: Mirrormere gives what she gives. She’s deep in the middle, mind. Deeper than the watchtower is tall, they say. Oh, and there’s one of Maren’s blue flowers on the shore yonder, if you’re collecting.
plan.say: Mirror-meer gives what she gives. She's deep in the middle, mind. Deeper than the watchtower is tall, they say. Oh, and there's one of Marren's blue flowers on the shore yonder, if you're collecting.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: A song for the traveller? I know nine. Seven of them are sad.
plan.say: A song for the traveller? I know nine. Seven of them are sad.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: This one’s called “The Road Goes Ever Up.” It isn’t about anything. The good ones never are.
plan.say: This one's called "The Road Goes Ever Up." It isn't about anything. The good ones never are.

plan.speaker: lark
plan.text: I came for one night, two winters ago. Greta’s ale is a kind of gravity.
plan.say: I came for one night, two winters ago. Gretta's ale is a kind of gravity.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: You walk loud.
plan.say: You walk loud.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: Forest edge, north-west of the gate. Another on the rocks above the river, north of the bridge. And one past my cabin, where the ground stays cold. Don’t trample them.
plan.say: Forest edge, north-west of the gate. Another on the rocks above the river, north of the bridge. And one past my cabin, where the ground stays cold. Don't trample them.

plan.speaker: wren
plan.text: Hare. Grouse. Silence, mostly.
plan.say: Hare. Grouse. Silence, mostly.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: Have you seen a chicken? Not for any reason.
plan.say: Have you seen a chicken? Not for any reason.

plan.speaker: pip
plan.text: My mum sells cloth and says I have to stay where she can see me. So I’m going to be a knight. Or a chicken farmer. I haven’t decided.
plan.say: My mum sells cloth and says I have to stay where she can see me. So I'm going to be a knight. Or a chicken farmer. I haven't decided.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Patrol’s quiet. Keep to the roads after dark, friend.
plan.say: Patrol's quiet. Keep to the roads after dark, friend.

plan.speaker: ivo
plan.text: Stonewater Bridge? Older than the village. Older than the chapel. Whoever built it meant for something to be on the other side.
plan.say: Stone-water Bridge? Older than the village. Older than the chapel. Whoever built it meant for something to be on the other side.

plan.speaker: hilda
plan.text: Wool from the high pastures, dyed with Maren’s roots. Feel that. Go on.
plan.say: Wool from the high pastures, dyed with Marren's roots. Feel that. Go on.

plan.speaker: hilda
plan.text: It keeps us fed. And if my Pip offers to sell you a chicken, it isn’t hers.
plan.say: It keeps us fed. And if my Pip offers to sell you a chicken, it isn't hers.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Apples! Cabbages! Oh. Sorry. Habit.
plan.say: Apples! Cabbages! Oh. Sorry. Habit.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Not a coin? Go on, then. Don’t tell Edda.
plan.say: Not a coin? Go on, then. Don't tell Edda.

plan.speaker: bram
plan.text: Best in the valley. Only in the valley, mind, but still.
plan.say: Best in the valley. Only in the valley, mind, but still.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Morning, traveller.
plan.say: Morning, traveller.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Keep to the road.
plan.say: Keep to the road.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Evening. Mind the dark.
plan.say: Evening. Mind the dark.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Late to be walking.
plan.say: Late to be walking.

plan.speaker: hale
plan.text: Put that blade away, friend.
plan.say: Put that blade away, friend.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Good morning, love.
plan.say: Good morning, love.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: There's stew on, if you're hungry.
plan.say: There's stew on, if you're hungry.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Come in, come in. There's a fire.
plan.say: Come in, come in. There's a fire.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Still up? Go on to bed.
plan.say: Still up? Go on to bed.

plan.speaker: greta
plan.text: Not in my house, thank you.
plan.say: Not in my house, thank you.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Morning.
plan.say: Morning.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Mind the sparks.
plan.say: Mind the sparks.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Done for the day, nearly.
plan.say: Done for the day, nearly.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Hm. Late.
plan.say: Hm. Late.

plan.speaker: brandt
plan.text: Careful with that. I made half of them.
plan.say: Careful with that. I made half of them.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Good morning, dear.
plan.say: Good morning, dear.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Take a look, take a look.
plan.say: Take a look, take a look.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Closing soon, dear.
plan.say: Closing soon, dear.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: We're shut, dear.
plan.say: We're shut, dear.

plan.speaker: marta
plan.text: Oh, put that away, do.
plan.say: Oh, put that away, do.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Peace of the morning.
plan.say: Peace of the morning.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Peace be with you.
plan.say: Peace be with you.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: The evening bell is near.
plan.say: The evening bell is near.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: Go gently, traveller.
plan.say: Go gently, traveller.

plan.speaker: aldous
plan.text: No blades in this place, please.
plan.say: No blades in this place, please.

plan.speaker: maren
plan.text: Up with the larks, are we?
plan.say: Up with the larks, are we?

plan.speaker: maren
